tagline: Under the bluffs, from one river mouth to another.
intro: The route starts at Hartford, near the mouth of the Missouri, where Lewis and Clark wintered at Camp River Dubois, and runs north 33 miles on the Great River Road. Above Alton it follows a chain of limestone bluffs with the Mississippi alongside and a bike trail beside the road, through Elsah and Grafton to the mouth of the Illinois.

The bluffs at Alton once carried a painted monster, which Marquette and Jolliet sketched in 1673 as a scaly beast with a man's face and a long fish-finned tail. The rock wall was probably destroyed in the 1850s. The creature has been repainted from copies several times since, and later pictures gave it wings.

moments.title: Elsah
moments.text: Its founder gave free lots to anyone who built with stone from his quarry, and in 1973 the whole village went onto the National Register.

moments.title: Grafton
moments.text: Its quarries sent limestone to build the Eads Bridge in St. Louis, and its boatworks turned out paddle wheelers and later PT boats.

moments.title: Pere Marquette State Park
moments.text: At the meeting of the Illinois and the Mississippi stands a lodge the Civilian Conservation Corps built in the 1930s, and in late winter hundreds of bald eagles gather here to fish.
